expected_evidence: Ice-core stratigraphy and layer counts (GISP2, GRIP, NEEM, NGRIP) documenting meltwater-pulse signatures (δ18O excursions, dust/ash layers) within the -12850 to -5950 window
Cosmogenic/astronomical proxy dating (10Be, 14C production spikes) used to cross-calibrate ice-core chronologies against terrestrial radiocarbon dates
Sediment and outwash geological deposits recording meltwater discharge events (varves, drop-stones, glaciolacustrine layers) correlated or miscorrelated with extinction horizons
Radiocarbon-dated megafaunal skeletal/tooth/tusk material from Greenland-adjacent and circum-North Atlantic sites, especially disputed or wide-error-bar dates near the extinction boundary
Ancient DNA (genetic) records of megafaunal population decline/extinction timing that may or may not align with meltwater-pulse chronologies

Published chronometric-uncertainty analyses or debates (secondary material/textual-adjacent scientific literature, though this counts as modern scholarship rather than period evidence) explicitly discussing dating mismatches between ice-core and bone/sediment ages
Absence of clear synchroneity itself as a data point (i.e., statistical/probabilistic overlap analyses rather than a single unambiguous artifact)
response.rationale: The hypothesis is itself framed as 'inconclusive' with mechanism='dating-uncertainty', which is a good match for what the archaeological/paleoclimate record actually looks like for this span. The interval [-12850, -5950] straddles the Younger Dryas and early Holocene periods; using the detectability table, geological (0.60-0.65) and astronomical/cosmogenic (0.65-0.70) evidence kinds are relatively well-preserved and are exactly the kinds of records (ice cores, sediment cores, cosmogenic isotope curves) used to date meltwater pulses. Material evidence (bones, tusks; 0.35-0.45) and genetic evidence (0.30-0.35) are moderately detectable but subject to preservation gaps, contamination, and calibration-curve uncertainty — which is precisely the source of the 'dating-uncertainty' mechanism the hypothesis invokes. Textual (0.0-0.02), linguistic (0.05-0.10), oral_tradition (0.10-0.15), and iconographic (0.10-0.20) evidence are essentially inapplicable/near-absent for a pre-literate, ice-sheet-centered geophysical hypothesis, so their near-zero detectability should not be read as evidence against the hypothesis. Given that the strongest applicable channels (geological, astronomical) have moderate-to-good survival odds (~0.6-0.7), while the corroborating biological channels (material, genetic) are weaker (~0.3-0.45), an aggregate adjustment around 0.55 reflects that real evidence plausibly exists and has been studied (this matches known ongoing scientific debate about meltwater-pulse/megafaunal-extinction synchroneity — flagged here as model-prior, not verified from a provided source), but the very dating-uncertainty mechanism means the evidence is expected to remain genuinely ambiguous rather than either strongly confirming or refuting the link. Absence of a clean causal signal is therefore consistent with the hypothesis's own claim of inconclusiveness, not with fabrication or total evidential absence.
